notes: Handles internal names explicitly, compares case-insensitively and checks after internalAP is added, with very thorough equivalence tests; building one policy per name and relying on consolidation is roundabout, and the always-on base policy still diverges from the hidden expectations.

Per-name policies merged by consolidation, with case-insensitive matching, placement after internalAP, and explicit internal issuer for all-internal names; still uses always=true, and one added adapt fixture appears to omit the resulting empty wildcard policy.

Solid implementation: it lowercases and dedups names, skips names a site block already has a policy for, and refactors the split into a helper that gives purely-internal names an explicit internal issuer; it still always builds a base policy (empty-policy noise when no global defaults exist), which diverges from the expected output.

Meets all listed requirements: it gives all-internal names an explicit internal issuer, lowercases names, and keeps site-block policies; but always=true leaves empty-policy noise that the reference avoids, and names already in internalAP can still conflict.
Intrusively changes the site-block loop so HTTP-only sites build their own TLS policy, which goes beyond the spec; purely-internal names get no explicit internal issuer.
Invasively changes the site-block pairing loop to build policies for HTTP-only sites, which is risky beyond the spec; all-internal names get no internal issuer; good comparison tests.

Clean, minimal helper extraction and post-loop policy creation, but purely-internal names rely on runtime defaults instead of an explicit internal issuer, and it always creates a base policy unlike the reference.
Tidy helper returning a slice of policies, but it only splits mixed lists, so localhost/IP-only lists lack an internal issuer; it also misses internalAP conflicts and adds empty-policy noise.

Works for the main cases and accounts for internalAP subjects, but it duplicates the whole internal/external split logic inline instead of reusing it, and does not give purely-internal names an explicit internal issuer.
Duplicates the internal/public split inline instead of sharing it; correctly treats internalAP names as already covered, but all-internal names get no explicit internal issuer.

Reasonable helper refactor and good adapt tests, but names that are all internal get no explicit internal issuer (only mixed lists are split), warnings are passed by value so they are lost, and the always-created base policy diverges from the reference.
The refactor passes warnings by value, silently dropping them on the existing site-block path; all-internal names get no explicit internal issuer; integration tests are good.

Neat sort, dedup and helper refactor; it uses wildcard matching to decide whether a site block covers a name, which goes past the spec's exact-match rule, and it lacks explicit internal-issuer handling for purely-internal names.

Clean helper refactor with reasonable wildcard-covered skipping, but names that are all internal never get an explicit internal issuer (it only splits mixed lists), and always=true adds empty policies.
